records.name: Queer Run
records.summary: A free run club for LGBTQIA+ runners in Philadelphia, run as a nonprofit. Runners of all paces meet for weekly runs in Center City and Manayunk.
records.what_you_do: Run three or four miles with other queer runners at your own pace, starting from a meeting point on a weekly run night.

schedule.text: Weekly runs: Mondays at 7 pm from the Center of Rittenhouse Square, Wednesdays at 6 pm from Philadelphia Runner in Manayunk, and Thursdays at 6 am from the southwest corner of Love Park

first_step.how: Show up at a meeting point on a run night. The site also has a Heylo invite link.
first_step.basis: All runs are free and open to all paces, and the site invites people to just show up.

records.notes: The site lists its next runs as 10/5, 10/7 and 10/8 with no year. The footer year is not used as evidence, so status is probably_active, not active.

records.name: Philadelphia Front Runners
records.summary: A running group for LGBT+ people and allies, active since 1983. It holds weekly runs and social events for all ages and paces.
records.what_you_do: Run a set route with others on Saturday mornings or Monday evenings, then join the brunch or social event that follows.

schedule.text: Saturdays at 9:30 am from Lloyd Hall, followed by brunch, and Mondays at 7 pm from the William Way Community Center for a 5 mile run through the historic district

first_step.how: Join the mailing list through the join section of the site, or come to a Saturday or Monday run
first_step.basis: Open to LGBT+ people and allies with a clear mailing list to join, though the site does not say how a first run works.

records.notes: The newest item on the site ('Meet a Front Runner') has no date. The only other dated reference is the 2018 Philly Pride Run. Email is only a contact form, so none is recorded.

records.name: West Philly Runners
records.summary: A West Philadelphia running club with a weekly group run in 2, 4 or 6 mile options and a Monday speed workout. It welcomes runners of many paces.
records.what_you_do: Join the Wednesday night group run at your pace, or the Monday speed workout if you want to train harder.

schedule.text: Weekly Wednesday night group run, and a Monday speed workout. Start times and meeting place are not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Use the JOIN US section on the site, which links to the club's Facebook group
first_step.basis: Welcomes many paces, but the site gives no sign up steps and no meeting place, so the way in is not clear.

records.notes: The newest post reads 'October 14 WPR Weekly Run' with no year. October 14 2026 falls on a Wednesday, which fits the weekly run, but the year is not stated, so it is not used as dated evidence.

records.name: South Philly Striders Running Club
records.summary: A running club for South Philadelphia, Penn's Landing, Old City and Queen Village. Its best known event is an annual holiday lights run that ends with a stop at a bar.
records.what_you_do: Join the holiday lights run in December with runners of all paces, then go to the bar afterward with the group.

schedule.text: Annual holiday lights run in December. The site lists a Thursday run at 7 pm from Marconi Plaza, at Broad Street and Oregon Avenue. Regular run times are not listed.

locations.label: Marconi Plaza, Broad Street and Oregon Avenue

first_step.how: Come to the holiday lights run; the site says all paces are welcome. Follow the club's Facebook group for news.
first_step.basis: The holiday run welcomes all paces, but the site lists no regular runs or sign up steps.

records.notes: The newest dated post is about the 18th annual holiday lights run and is dated 2025-11-24. The page gives December 11 without a year. Regular weekly runs are not listed on the site.

records.name: Wynnefield Track Club
records.summary: A group of training partners who run weekly sessions for health and wellness. It welcomes runners of every level and meets at Lloyd Hall and at St. Joseph's University.
records.what_you_do: Show up for a Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday or Sunday run, or the Tuesday track workout, and run with the group.

schedule.text: Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 5:30 am at Lloyd Hall. Tuesday track at 5:30 am and 6:30 pm at Sweeney Field. Thursday tempo runs at 5:30 am at Lloyd Hall and 6:30 pm at the Cynwyd Heritage Trail. Saturday long runs at 6 am and Sunday at 6:30 am, both at Lloyd Hall.

first_step.how: Just show up at a session, or sign up for the email newsletter
first_step.basis: The site says to just show up and that all levels are welcome.

records.notes: The site lists a full weekly schedule, but the only dated item is a 2020 'coming soon' placeholder. The schedule may be out of date, so this is marked dormant until someone confirms the runs are still happening. Meeting spots are said to be updated on social media.

records.name: Issa Run Crew
records.summary: A Philadelphia running crew that trains together and celebrates goals, open to runners of any distance or pace.
records.what_you_do: Join a Monday evening easy 3.1 mile run from Whole Foods on Pennsylvania Avenue, a Thursday track session at Temple, or a Saturday morning run from Lloyd Hall followed by coffee and donuts.

schedule.text: Monday Night Therapy: meet at 5:45 pm, run at 6 pm. Track Thursday at Temple Sports Complex, start time not stated. Saturday run starts at 8 am from Lloyd Hall.

first_step.how: Show up at a run. The site says to just show up.
first_step.basis: The site says all paces are welcome and gives the meeting spots, though it describes no sign up steps.

records.notes: The site has no dated posts or events. Its only date-like item is an image upload stamp, which is not used.

records.name: Philadelphia Runner Track Club
records.summary: A competitive training club for post-collegiate runners, founded in 2000, with coaching, training groups and sponsorship support. It has over 200 runners.
records.what_you_do: Train in groups on Tuesday track workouts and Sunday long runs, split by distance and pace, after the club accepts you.

schedule.text: Track Tuesday at 6:30 pm, at Franklin Field or the Temple Sports Complex. Sunday long run at 9 am from Lloyd Hall, earlier in summer.

locations.label: Franklin Field or Temple Sports Complex

cost.text: Not stated on the site, including any dues

first_step.how: Apply through the Apply or Run With Us page. Applications are closed until the next round opens on January 1, 2027.
first_step.basis: Membership needs an application and a set time standard, and applications are closed until January 2027.

records.notes: Age and university status are not stated. The site shows no post dates. The next application round is the only dated item, and it is in the future. Recorded as an application club, not an open drop in run.

records.name: Men's Night Run Club Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that uses running, wellness efforts and community events to support men's physical health, mental well-being and friendships. It is open to men 18 and up.
records.what_you_do: Sign up on the site, register for a weekly night run through the event page, and run with other men.

schedule.text: Weekly night runs. Days and start times are not listed on the site. Event details and registration are on Eventbrite.

first_step.how: Fill out the Join Men's Night Run Club sign up form on the site, then register for a run through the Eventbrite link
first_step.basis: Open to men 18 and up with a sign up form and public event registration, though the site does not describe what a run is like.

records.notes: No dated posts or events on the site. The copyright footer is not used as evidence. An earlier list gave a meeting address on South 11th Street that the site itself does not confirm, so no location is recorded.

records.name: Students Run Philly Style
records.summary: A free Philadelphia nonprofit that pairs students in grades 6 to 12 with adult volunteer mentors, called Running Leaders, to train for half or full marathons together.
records.what_you_do: Students and mentors train together up to 10 hours a week from March through November, building toward a race. Mentors volunteer as Running Leaders.

schedule.text: Students and mentors train up to 10 hours a week, March through November.

cost.text: Free for students, according to the program description

first_step.how: Use the Become a Student Runner page or the Become a Volunteer Mentor page
first_step.basis: Students and mentors apply through set pages, and the steps are not spelled out on the site.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a link to a 2025-11-21 Inquirer article. The date is taken from the link address, not the article text. Mentor age requirement is not stated, so the mentor age is not recorded. Practice days and times are not listed.

records.name: Philly Girls Who Walk
records.summary: A free community for women in Philadelphia that organizes walks, outdoor activities and social events so members can stay active and meet people.
records.what_you_do: Join group walks and outdoor events with other women in the city, signing up through the group's Heylo page.

schedule.text: Upcoming walks and events are listed on the group's Heylo page. Days and times are not shown on the website itself.

first_step.how: Click Join us on the site, which goes to the group's Heylo page
first_step.basis: Free and open to women in Philadelphia with a clear sign up link, though the website itself lists no dates.

records.notes: The site has no dated events. The upcoming list is on the Heylo page, which was not read. A photo caption mentions a free yoga session on the Art Museum lawn, undated, so yoga is not recorded as an interest.

records.name: Girls on the Run Philadelphia
records.summary: A program for girls in grades 3 to 5 and grades 6 to 8, called Heart and Sole for the older group, that mixes running with life skills lessons. Each season ends with a 5K, and volunteer coaches lead the lessons.
records.what_you_do: Girls meet in teams with volunteer coaches for lessons and running, and train toward a 5K at the end of the season.

schedule.text: Team lessons each season, ending in a 5K. Days and times are not stated on the site.

locations.label: Organization office (team sites not listed on the site)

cost.text: Cost to girls not stated on the site

first_step.how: Read the 3rd to 5th grade or 6th to 8th grade program pages, or contact the office to find a team
first_step.basis: The site does not describe how to register, and the way in runs through team sign ups.

records.notes: The only date on the page is the footer copyright, which is not used as evidence. Volunteer coach need and age requirement are not stated. The site also has a Start a Team page for new locations.

records.name: Bicycle Club of Philadelphia
records.summary: An all-volunteer nonprofit that promotes biking in the Philadelphia area and runs free group rides for every speed and skill level.
records.what_you_do: Pick a ride from the club's ride calendar at your speed and join it. Come to the monthly club meeting if you want to get more involved.

schedule.text: Recurring weekly rides on a published ride calendar at all speeds. Monthly club meeting on the second Wednesday at 6:30 pm, unless noted otherwise.

cost.text: Group rides are free. Membership dues are not stated.

first_step.how: Find a ride on the ride calendar and show up. The club says everyone is welcome. Join the club through its Join BCP link.
first_step.basis: The site says everyone is welcome to rides and gives a clear link to join the club.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a 'BCP at the Shore Weekend' from October 16 to 19 with no year, so it is not used as evidence. Ride pace groups and sign up for individual rides are not stated.

records.name: We Walk PHL
records.summary: A free walking group that meets in city parks and is led by trained neighborhood residents. It is supported by the Fairmount Park Conservancy, the city Department of Public Health and Parks and Recreation.
records.what_you_do: Walk about an hour with neighbors in a city park, led by a trained local resident. Register through the sign up portal or check the Facebook group for the week's spot.

schedule.text: Sites host one to three walks a week in season. Bartram's Garden walks ran on Thursdays at 5 pm in spring 2026. Fall 2026 dates were not found.

first_step.how: Register through the GivePulse portal (recommended, per the event page) or check the We Walk PHL Facebook group for current spots
first_step.basis: Free walks for people of all ages and abilities, with a sign up portal and a posted meeting place.

records.notes: The city post is dated 2025-09-10 and describes the fall season of September 1 to October 31. The Bartram's Garden event page for 2026-06-18 is the newest dated item. Sites in other neighborhoods are posted on Facebook and were not confirmed here. The website recorded is the program's sign up portal, not a separate program site.

records.name: Philly Track Jawn
records.summary: A Philadelphia community group that runs free, inclusive running and walking sessions led by certified coaches, to support health, fitness and connection.
records.what_you_do: Join a free Tuesday track workout at the Temple University Sports Complex, with sessions built for different fitness levels. Weekend runs and walks are also offered.

schedule.text: Free track workouts on Tuesdays at 7 pm at the Temple University Sports Complex. Thursday 6 pm session also listed. Weekend run and walk times are not stated.

cost.text: Free for the weekly Tuesday track workouts. Weekend cost not stated.

first_step.how: Fill in the Sign Up Here form linked on the site
first_step.basis: Open to all with sessions for different fitness levels, and a clear sign up form.

records.notes: The page shows no dated posts. Its 'page updated' date is not displayed. The Thursday session is listed in the page text, but the time is not given.

records.name: Mural Miles
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs group runs past public art around Philadelphia. The group stops at each piece to talk about it, and the runs are social, educational and open to all fitness levels.
records.what_you_do: Run or walk a monthly route past public art with a group, pausing at each piece to talk about it.

schedule.text: Monthly group runs. Dates and times are posted on Instagram rather than on the website.

first_step.how: Read the FAQ page or follow the calendar on Instagram
first_step.basis: The site says runs suit all fitness levels, but the sign up path is only through the FAQ and Instagram.

records.notes: Instagram posts are shown without dates on the site, so status is not confirmed by a dated item. The cost and the sign up steps are not stated on the site.

records.name: Neighborhood Bike Works
records.summary: A nonprofit community bike shop at 3939 Lancaster Avenue. It teaches people to ride and repair bikes, and sells refurbished bikes and parts to pay for free and low-cost classes.
records.what_you_do: Fix your own bike with the shop's tools during Bike Church or an open shop night, or join the youth program to learn repair.

schedule.text: Community shop open Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 12 to 4 pm. Bike Church (18 and up) on Tuesday and Thursday from 6:30 to 9 pm, and the first Saturday from 3 to 6 pm. Women, trans and nonbinary open shop (18 and up) on Wednesday from 6:30 to 9 pm. Youth programs Monday to Thursday from 4 to 6 pm, and a Saturday youth drop in from 10 am to 2 pm for youth graduates.

cost.text: Shop prices and class fees are not stated on the site

first_step.how: Youth: fill in the Youth Programs Interest Form on the site. Adults: come to Bike Church or an open shop hour.
first_step.basis: The shop teaches people to ride and repair bikes, has open hours for adults, and has a clear youth interest form.

records.notes: The site has no dated events or news. The Wednesday open shop is for women, trans and nonbinary people 18 and up, which is why women and transgender are recorded as the community. The site lists both 3939 Lancaster Ave (shop) and 3943 Lancaster Ave (mailing address); 3939 is recorded as the shop.

records.name: Liberty Track Club
records.summary: A post-collegiate women's running club in Philadelphia for athletes training for national level races, from the 800 meters to the marathon.
records.what_you_do: Train with a competitive group of women runners working toward national championship and Olympic Trials qualifying times.

cost.text: Membership cost not stated on the site

first_step.how: Email the club. The site does not describe how to join.
first_step.basis: A competitive club for post-collegiate athletes, and the site shows no steps to join.

records.notes: No training schedule, meeting place or join process is shown on the site. Posts mention races and a Berlin marathon, but none carry a full date. A Billy Penn list gave a membership fee and timing standards that the site does not confirm, so they are not recorded.

records.name: T3 Philly Multisport
records.summary: A Philadelphia triathlon and multisport club founded in 2003. It offers group workouts, clinics, coaching and social events for members of many abilities.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member to take part in group workouts, clinics and social events with people of many abilities.

cost.text: Membership price not shown on the site

first_step.how: Use the Become a T3 Philly Member button to reach the membership page
first_step.basis: The site says all levels are welcome and that it is always looking for new members, with a sign up page.

records.notes: No schedule, meeting place or dated post on the site. Photo file names contain 2023 dates, but those are race result photos, not club events, so they are not used. The page names no sport beyond multisport, so only running is recorded as an interest.

records.name: Bicycle Coalition
records.summary: A nonprofit advocacy group for safer biking and walking in Philadelphia. It runs youth cycling and learn to ride programs, group rides and advocacy walks for safer streets.
records.what_you_do: Join a learn to ride class, a group ride, or an advocacy walk for safer streets. Young people can take part in the youth cycling program.

schedule.text: Group rides, learn to ride classes and advocacy walks run through the year. Dates are on the site's classes and rides pages, which were not readable in this pass.

cost.text: Costs not stated on the page read

first_step.how: Call the office, or check the classes and rides page on the site
first_step.basis: Program details are on linked pages that were not readable, so the way in is not clear from the page read.

records.notes: A post refers to the 2026 Eastern Pennsylvania Greenways and Trails Summit in September, which sets the evidence month. A Sept 27 advocacy walk is listed with no year; its date is only inferred from the weekday, so it is not used. Advocacy work is nonpartisan.

records.name: Ben Franklin Mob H3
records.summary: A Philadelphia hash running group. A rotating hare lays a trail, and runners follow it at any pace, often in costume.
records.what_you_do: Follow a marked trail laid by a rotating hare at your own pace. Bring $10 in Hash Cash and photo ID.

schedule.text: Thursday trails: gather at 7 pm and run at 7:30 pm. The meeting place changes from trail to trail.

cost.text: Bring $10 in Hash Cash. The site does not say what it covers.

first_step.how: Follow the New? Click here link on the site to the About page, or email the group
first_step.basis: All faces and paces are welcome, and the site has a newcomer link, though it gives no other sign up steps.

records.notes: The trail is listed for Thursday 10/8 with no year. The latest dated item is a Marathon Beer Check on 2026-11-22, a future event. The site gives the trail address as 37 E Palmer St, but its map link says 37 W Palmer St. Confirm before publishing the address.

records.name: EarlyBirds and NightOwls
records.summary: Two Philadelphia area run groups, an early morning group and a night group, run through Recovery Run Coaching. They run roads and trails in different spots and focus on community.
records.what_you_do: Run roads and trails with the group, checking each group's Instagram page for the week's route and time.

first_step.how: Follow the EarlyBirds or NightOwls Instagram page to see upcoming runs
first_step.basis: The way in is through social media, and the site gives no sign up steps or schedule.

records.notes: Times and places are posted only on Instagram, and the site has no dated items. The site does not say whether the groups are for people in recovery or for any runners, so no audience is recorded. Email is the coaching business address.

notes: Budget: all 10 WebSearch calls were used, so the search budget is exhausted. About 49 fetches. 21 records written, all verdict publish. Coverage: running, walking and bike groups are well covered. Yoga, martial arts and strength training produced no publishable group in this pass: the free outdoor yoga and workout listings I found are 2014 to 2019 articles or lack a current source, and the martial arts leads are a 2023 unvetted listing and 2021 news. These are in leads_only for future research. Business excluded: Furthur Training and Racing (endurance coaching business; its site lists no community program or schedule). Out of area and not recorded: Conshohocken Running, RUNegades, Central Bucks Bicycle Club, Delaware Valley Bicycle Club, West Chester groups. Wellness on the Waterfront and the Dilworth Park yoga listing had no checked website. Several records are probably_active because the site is working but shows no dated items. Only dated evidence sets active or dormant. Address conflict flagged in Ben Franklin Mob H3 notes.
